mission.title: Good Manners
mission.description: Ask three powerful Exiles for a kill code for the Oracle.

npc.say: She has tasted my vengeance once before... I do not think she is foolish enough to want to feel it again.
Flood will provide you with further details as you require them.
Tell you what, next time you stop by Club Noir, the drinks are on me, all right?

I do have certain information concerning the predecessor that the Merovingian might be interested in...
Well, perhaps some other time, then.
I do not say that the Merovingian is wrong, merely that there are few who are prepared to walk that road with him.

phase.briefing:
Oh, it's you. I knew the day was going too well.
The Merovingian wants to see you. It's about the Oracle, of course.

enter.say: If you've got a breath mint, now would be a good time to use it!

talk.say:
I've had it. So, the Oracle will not deal with me--then I will deal with her! Once I have a kill code for her current shell, she'll have to accept my terms.
I do not at present have such a code, but that is a minor detail. We will procure one somewhere.

done.say: I think that's your cue to hit up Malphas there for your instructions.

talk.say:
The Machine program from whom we obtained the termination code used on the Oracle previously is very unlikely to have access to one for her current shell; in any case, Rama-Kandra has no further need of buying our services.
Therefore, we must look elsewhere to find such a code. We will first approach certain powerful Exiles. You, {player}, are scheduled to meet with the Bartender, Hypatia, and the Network. Each of these has certain unique contacts which may give them access to the requisite code.

phase.briefing:
Your first meeting is with the Exile known as "The Bartender." Do not accept any drinks from her--they're positively awful.
The Bartender has somehow carved out a neutral niche in the Matrix. It is generally supposed that she achieved this thanks to some kind of agreement with Deus Ex Machina. It sounds like a ridiculous rumor, if you ask me, but in any case, she may have some contact in the Machine world that would allow her to obtain a kill code for the fortune teller.

enter.say: The Bartender should be in there. I'm scanning a single strong Exile program.

talk.say: You must be joking. Even if I knew where to get a kill code for her--which I don't--my interest lies in preserving the peace, not in wrecking it, and killing the author of the Truce would probably be the best way to ruin the Pax Oracula, hm?

done.say: Bah! As I expected, a worthless program.

phase.briefing: Now you will meet with Hypatia. She hordes a great deal of information in her private library; it is also said that she was a member, perhaps even a founding member, of the Archivist Society, which could mean that she has experience bridging constructs and servers. In any case, she may have the means to locate the code we seek.

enter.say: That's where you're supposed to meet her. I'm picking up multiple readings in there; those may be her Bookwyrm guards.

talk.say: I am flattered that the Merovingian thinks I might have access to a kill code for the Oracle, but such a thing would be of little actual interest to a researcher such as myself. Facts and fictions, rather than weapons, are my fascination. I know nothing of such a code.

done.say: I knew it; these so-called "mighty" are nothing more than masters of worthless trivia! They will never progress farther than the squalid little tracts of land they pretend to rule.

phase.briefing: Hmph. I will admit that your next contact, the Exile called "The Network," has a certain amount of power, at least among bluepills. We know that he provides the Architect with media streams in return for his broadcast monopoly in the city. He may have the information resources and pull necessary to obtain a kill code for the Oracle, if the price is right.

enter.say: I'm reading multiple programs in there. One of them should be the Network.
Hm, the far door is sealed shut. Those guys there must be his guards. Whoops, watch it! They're attacking!

done.say: The other door just unlocked. Was that some kind of test?

talk.say:
Oh, it is you. One cannot be too careful, these days.
In regards to your inquiry, I am neither interested in rendering the Frenchman such assistance, nor do I have the means to do so.
If I may offer a bit of advice... I very much doubt that you will find anyone else in a position of power within the city who is willing to assist in terminating the Oracle. You would do better to look elsewhere; or, better yet, give up the endeavor entirely.

done.say: Bloated buffoon! He is right about one thing, at least: we are wasting our time with the city's riff-raff, as I have been saying all along.

mission.finish: Perhaps after these remarkable failures the Merovingian will deign to give more weight to my counsel. Malphas always thinks he knows everything... Well, he may know the city, but he has precious little conception of anything beyond that, as I'm sure even you have noticed by now.
